name: nassaj-dev
description: nassaj-dev — claudecodeui fork with AntigravityProvider and RTL Arabic support

scripts.test: npm run test:server; s=$?; npm run test:src; c=$?; if [ $s -ne 0 ] || [ $c -ne 0 ]; then exit 1; fi
scripts.test:src: node -e 'const{globSync,readFileSync}=require("node:fs");const f=globSync("src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}").filter(p=>/from .node:test./.test(readFileSync(p,"utf8")));if(!f.length){console.log("test:src: no node:test files under src/");process.exit(0)}const r=require("node:child_process").spawnSync("npx",["tsx","--experimental-test-module-mocks","--test",...f],{stdio:"inherit"});process.exit(r.status===null?1:r.status)'
scripts.build: npm run build:client && npm run build:server
scripts.lint: eslint src/ server/ shared/ scripts/ commitlint.config.js postcss.config.js tailwind.config.js vite.config.js eslint.config.js ecosystem.config.example.cjs --report-unused-disable-directives-severity=warn --max-warnings=460
scripts.lint:fix: eslint src/ server/ shared/ scripts/ commitlint.config.js postcss.config.js tailwind.config.js vite.config.js eslint.config.js ecosystem.config.example.cjs --fix
scripts.start: npm run build && npm run server

author: CloudCLI UI Contributors

nassajTestIsolation.why: JSON forbids comments, so the reasoning behind the DATABASE_PATH prefix on the `test:server` script lives here. In a shell that does NOT already export DATABASE_PATH, server/load-env.js:20 injects it from .env (`if (!process.env[key])`), and .env:16 on a deployed node points at the LIVE production SQLite file. So `npm test` was not self-contained: its outcome depended on the caller's environment, and the ONLY thing standing between a plain `npm test` and the production database was assertTestDatabaseIsIsolated (connection.ts), which throws before the connection is opened. The script now defaults DATABASE_PATH itself so the ambient value can never be production.
nassajTestIsolation.shape: DATABASE_PATH="${DATABASE_PATH:-$(mktemp -d)/auth.db}" — three properties, all deliberate: (1) `mktemp -d` honours $TMPDIR and otherwise lands in /tmp, which are exactly the roots assertTestDatabaseIsIsolated trusts (connection.ts:176-186); (2) it is UNIQUE per invocation, so two concurrent runs cannot collide and no run inherits state from a previous one; (3) `${VAR:-default}` only substitutes when unset or empty, so an explicit caller override is still honoured.
nassajTestIsolation.notCleanedUp: Each run leaves one small temp directory behind. Cleaning it would mean an `rm -rf` on a shell-expanded variable inside a JSON one-liner, which is a worse risk than a few hundred KB under /tmp that the OS tmpfiles policy reclaims anyway.
nassajTestIsolation.testSrcExempt: test:src is deliberately NOT wrapped: it runs the node:test files under src/, none of which import server/modules/database, load-env or getConnection (verified by grep), and it passes in a clean shell with DATABASE_PATH unset. Adding a temp dir there would be cargo-cult.
nassajTestIsolation.loadBearingTests: server/routes/settings.push-unsubscribe.test.ts and server/routes/tests/branding-logo.test.ts are the two files that can reach getConnection() during module evaluation, via auth.js:42 `const JWT_SECRET = resolveJwtSecret()` falling through to appConfigDb.getOrCreateJwtSecret() when process.env.JWT_SECRET is absent. Whether they trip the guard depends on whether JWT_SECRET happens to be set at import time — which is why they fail on some machines and pass on others. This script change removes the production path from that equation; the load-order fragility inside those two files is a separate issue, recorded but not fixed here.

nassajLintBudget.note: JSON forbids comments, so the ratchet plan for the --max-warnings ceiling in the `lint` script lives here. 441 warnings measured on src/+server/+shared/+scripts/+root configs (0 errors). The 460 ceiling is ~4% headroom so today's tree passes while genuine growth is blocked. Plan: lower the ceiling to the freshly measured count after each cleanup wave; never raise it without an ADR. 379 of the 441 are eslint --fix-able (import-x/order + tailwindcss/classnames-order) but a bulk --fix is deliberately NOT run while parallel sessions hold uncommitted work.
nassajLintBudget.unusedDisableDirectives: 11 stale eslint-disable directives exist; the CLI flag is pinned to --report-unused-disable-directives-severity=warn because the plain --report-unused-disable-directives form raises them to errors and would fail the build today. Flip it to error once those 11 are removed.
nassajLintBudget.blocked: Expanding eslint.config.js with an actual rules block for shared/, scripts/ and root files is blocked by the config-protection hook (nassaj-core/hooks/config-protection.js). Until that is lifted those paths are in argv but match no config block, so they are effectively rule-free.
